newsitem.title: ITALY: Black teenager crowned Miss Italy after racism storm.
newsitem.headline: Black teenager crowned Miss Italy after racism storm.

text.p: An 18-year-old black beauty has been crowned Miss Italy after a storm over alleged racism on the jury.
Denny Mendez, from Dominican Republic in the Caribbean, won the contest televised live on Saturday night with the help of an overwhelming nine million telephone votes from viewers.
Newspapers splashed her triumph across their front pages on Sunday after four days of rows in the media over whether a black could represent Italian beauty.

One member of the jury, photographer Bob Krieger, was thrown off the panel after insisting the answer was "no" and another, showbusiness personality Alba Parietti, was ousted in his wake after springing to his support.
Parietti, a former Miss Universe contestant, was re-instated to the jury and as "Mother Hen" to the contestants on Saturday after a flurry of last minute negotiations.
She placed the crown on Mendez's carefully coiffeured head on Saturday night and embraced the winner.

A tearful Mendez made all the right noises about hoping to finish her studies in tourism before starting work but drew a smattering of jeers and catcalls from the audience when she said she did not think the row over race had helped her chances.
"I still can't believe it. I really didn't think I'd win," she said.
"I'm not bothered about the whistles. I feel Italian," La Repubblica newspaper quoted her as saying on Sunday.
Mendez moved from the Dominican capital, Santo Domingo, to Italy with her mother and is a naturalised Italian. Her stepfather is Italian.
Mendez had written in her application to take part that she wanted to compete "to see what effect having a coloured girl among the competitors has".
The storm her involvement unleashed was fired when Krieger declared that "a black woman can't win a competition that's meant to reward and represent Italic beauty".
"Let's make her Miss Universe but not Miss Italy," he said.

Parietti, whose political views and physique once led her to be described by an Italian magazine as the "long thigh" of the left, said her remarks in support of Krieger had been misconstrued to portray her unjustly as a racist.
"Denny doesn't represent Italian beauty but that doesn't mean she can't take part in Miss Italy," she said.

Examples of violent racism are rare in Italy though the problem has been highlighted by occasional disturbances among Italians and immigrants, many of them illegal, from North Africa in rundown areas of many cities.
